text:
Maya: ran an nsys + perfetto sweep on the 8xA100 perf cluster for the pipeline workload (seq=2048, batcher=adaptive). Seeing 180-240ms tail spikes on pod-7. attaching traces. low-level looks like allreduce overlapping with big matmuls.
Zheng: can you upload the nsys? which commit did this start after — b4c3f9a?
Maya: yes b4c3f9a (kernel-routing rewrite). nsys: s3://perf/1947654321_maya.ns.gz. perfetto: https://perfetto/r/abc123. nvprof snippets below — batcher occasionally emits oversized combined batches (~512-768 tokens).
Eli: quick skim: nvprof shows matmul_batched_fp16 jump to ~40ms on GPU3. nccl timeline shows allreduce starting during matmul -> serialized allreduce on GPU0. could be communicator reuse + stream overlap.
Ana: @Maya can you paste the NVTX ranges around the batcher flush and kv retire counts?
Maya: NVTX snippet:
```
[BATCHER] flush xfer start
[KERNEL] matmul_fp16_slab
[KERNEL] kv_handshake_retro
[COMM] ncclAllReduce
```
KV retire log: "kv_retire: 24318 entries, avg_stride=128, retire_ms=7.2, spikes at 186ms"
perf-bot: perf regression alert: +2.3% tail vs baseline (2026-01-21). flagged selector fallbacks to generic gemm for some shapes. :warning:
Zheng: repro script suggestion: RUN_SEQ=2048 BATCHER=adaptive MAKE_COMM=separate; capture NVTX + nsys with --capture-range=nvtx. also try NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 to get async traces.
Eli: hypothesis: batching heuristic merges variable-length samples -> creates large matmuls that don't hit optimized kernel paths -> kernel selector falls back to generic_gemm. also nccl/allreduce launches overlap with kv handshake causing syncs.
Ana: also see kv handshake queued during allreduce window; search trace for 'stream 4 sync' — might be a cudaStreamSynchronize in the retire path.
Maya: found: 'cudaStreamSynchronize(stream=4) @ 0x7fb... right before nccl launch on GPU3'
Zheng: b4c3f9a changed default stream assignment for KV retire -> may have moved ops onto comm stream. quick patch: move KV retire to low-priority stream and re-run. anyone can run patched build?
Eli: i'll spin a canary with KV on low-prio stream, set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and capture nsys. if latency drops it's the stream sync.
Ana: also try NCCL_GROUP / single collective per step and cap combined batch size: export REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS=4096. that should keep matmul sizes in optimized regime.
Maya: ran canary with KV->low-prio: tail dropped from ~210ms to ~120ms in prelim. still see rare 90ms spikes when batcher emits ~768-token jobs. logs show 'selector: fallback_count=12 -> generic_gemm'.
perf-bot: TL;DR: root cause likely batching heuristic producing oversized shapes + selector mismatch + KV ops colliding with NCCL on same stream. suggested actions: 1) revert stream assignment in b4c3f9a (short-term), 2) add selector telemetry (mid-term), 3) enforce batch cap config (prod), 4) add perf bench for seq512/2048 combos.
deploy-bot: canary build deployed to perf-canary-3 with KV stream fix — https://deploys/3
Zheng: i'll open a PR with telemetry + small batching heuristic tweak to prefer earlier flush when seq variance high. assigning reviewers @Eli @Ana.
Eli: ack, will review today. also add NVLINK bandwidth checks — seen occasional link flaps that correlate with allreduce elongation on the trace.
Ana: i'll add an eval that mixes short+long sequences to ensure selector keeps optimized kernel coverage.
Maya: thanks everyone — i'll attach perfetto slices and the nvprof scripts to the PR and leave the raw traces in S3. follow-up in the issue.
